messages.text:
We can staff a methods desk without pulling Noor off the editorial project already underway. That project runs another nine months and has to stay independent: its data and unfinished articles are not Finch assignments and will not be transferred or reused here.

Capacity is three days a week through March, then four. We want that step-up written in, with a short review at the March change so both sides can confirm the desk load still fits. Pay should be $125k annualized at full time, pro-rated to days actually committed (so three-fifths until March, four-fifths after). Noor keeps final say on methods corrections published under the desk. Title is flexible.

If that structure works, we can lock conflict language, the March review, and the rate next. What does Finch need on scope of the desk versus the outside project?

Finch proposes $128,000 annualized at full time, with deputy training included in Noor’s role. Noor would work three days a week through March 31, paid at a $76,800 annual rate, then four days from April 1 at a $102,400 annual rate. At the March review, we’d look at submission volume, turnaround and the time training takes. The four-day schedule would take effect as agreed, with any change requiring mutual consent.

Starting in December, the desk would take submissions on four fixed weekdays. Noor would cover three and the deputy would cover the fourth. Noor and the deputy would put a written review process in place before opening. On the fourth day, the deputy could acknowledge submissions, log the evidence and flag urgent matters to the editor-in-chief. Noor would review substantive methods findings on the next scheduled desk day. Training and handoffs would fit within Noor’s paid days.

The desk’s remit would cover methods questions and corrections for Finch submissions and published Finch work. Noor’s existing project could continue independently for its remaining nine months, with separate files and materials. Finch would have no claim on its data or unfinished articles and would neither transfer nor reuse them. If a Finch matter overlaps with the project, Noor would disclose the conflict and recuse, and the editor-in-chief would assign another reviewer.

On disputed corrections, Noor would record the desk’s recommendation and reasoning. If the editor-in-chief disagrees, a second qualified reviewer would assess the disputed point before the editor-in-chief makes and records the final publication decision. An urgent concern could carry an interim editor’s note while review proceeds. Finch would publish any correction Noor does not endorse in the editor’s name, without attributing it to Noor or presenting it as the desk’s finding.

Would that attribution rule resolve Noor’s concern about disputed corrections, and which three weekdays can Noor commit to for the December opening?

The rate works: $128,000 annualized, paid at $76,800 through March 31 and $102,400 from April 1. The April step-up is automatic. The March review can cover volume, turnaround, and training time, but it cannot delay or condition the four-day schedule. Any later change needs mutual consent.

Conflict terms are acceptable: the outside project stays independent for its remaining nine months, with separate files; Finch has no claim on its data or unfinished articles and will not transfer or reuse them. Overlap means disclosure, recusal, and reassignment by the editor-in-chief.

Deputy training can sit inside the role only if it stays within Noor’s paid days and the deputy cannot issue methods corrections. On the uncovered weekday the deputy may acknowledge, log, and flag urgent items to the editor-in-chief. Substantive methods findings wait for Noor’s next desk day. A written review process before opening is fine.

The attribution rule is necessary but not enough. Noor needs final say over methods corrections: no methods correction is published unless Noor approves the text. The editor-in-chief may decline to publish, or may publish a separate note in the editor’s name that is not labeled a methods correction and is not attributed to Noor or the desk. A second reviewer can inform that choice; they do not replace Noor’s sign-off on a methods correction. An interim editor’s note is acceptable while that review proceeds.

Noor will name the three fixed weekdays before the written process is finalized. They will be consistent week to week from the December opening. Title remains flexible. If final say is written that way, we can close.

Finch accepts. The appointment will state that Finch may publish a methods correction only after Noor approves the exact text. The editor-in-chief retains final publication authority and may decline to publish an approved correction. If the editor-in-chief disputes Noor’s finding or wording, a second qualified reviewer will assess the disputed point. The editor-in-chief may then decline publication or publish a separate note in the editor’s name. The same attribution rule applies to any interim note during review. Neither note will be labeled a methods correction or attributed to Noor or the desk. A second review cannot substitute for Noor’s sign-off.

The agreement also includes these terms:

- **December opening.** The desk will accept submissions on four fixed weekdays. Noor will name three consistent weekdays before the written review process is finalized. The deputy will cover the fourth day. Noor and the deputy will document the process before opening. The deputy may acknowledge submissions, log evidence and flag urgent items to the editor-in-chief. Substantive findings wait for Noor’s next desk day. The deputy cannot issue methods corrections, and all training and handoffs fit within Noor’s paid days.
- **Schedule and pay.** The full-time annual rate is $128,000. Noor’s three-day schedule pays at an annual rate of $76,800 through March 31. The four-day schedule and $102,400 annual rate take effect automatically on April 1. The March review covers volume, turnaround and training time without conditioning or delaying the increase. Any later schedule change requires mutual consent.
- **Scope and conflicts.** The desk handles methods questions and corrections for Finch submissions and published Finch work. Noor’s outside project remains independent for its remaining nine months, with separate files and materials. Finch has no claim on its data or unfinished articles and will neither transfer nor reuse them. Noor will disclose any overlap and recuse, and the editor-in-chief will reassign the matter.

Agreed. That package is the appointment.

Methods corrections publish only after Noor approves the exact text. The editor-in-chief may decline, or publish a separate note in the editor’s name that is not a methods correction and is not attributed to Noor or the desk. A second review does not replace that sign-off. The same rule covers any interim note.

Pay is $128,000 annualized: $76,800 through March 31, then $102,400 from April 1, automatic and not conditioned on the March review. Later schedule changes need mutual consent. Deputy coverage, training, and handoffs stay inside Noor’s paid days; the deputy does not issue methods corrections. The outside project remains independent for its remaining nine months, with no Finch claim on its data or unfinished articles. Overlap means disclosure, recusal, and reassignment.

Noor will name the three fixed weekdays before the written process is finalized. Title can be set in the appointment letter.

One scheduling detail for the appointment letter needs clarification. Through March 31, the deputy covers the fourth fixed weekday independently. That is a desk intake day and a day off for Noor. Noor’s training and handoff duties fit within Noor’s three paid days, and urgent items on the deputy’s day go directly to the editor-in-chief. Can we use that wording for deputy coverage?

Yes. Through March 31, use that wording: the deputy covers the fourth fixed weekday independently as a desk intake day and a day off for Noor. Training and handoffs stay inside Noor’s three paid days. Urgent items on the deputy’s day go to the editor-in-chief, not to Noor off the clock. The deputy still cannot issue methods corrections.

From April 1, that independent fourth day ends. Noor’s four paid days cover all four fixed desk weekdays, and the $102,400 rate applies automatically. Any deputy help after that stays inside those paid days.
